question: Which of the following pairs correctly represents the cropping season and its corresponding time of sowing?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kharif June to September**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kharif season** in India is primarily associated with the **Southwest Monsoon**, which provides the necessary rainfall for these moisture-heavy crops. Hence, **Kharif - June to September** is correct.
 
• Sowing typically begins in **June** with the onset of rains, and the harvesting process takes place between **September and October**.
 
• Major **Kharif crops** include **Rice**, **Maize**, **Jowar**, **Bajra**, **Tur** (Arhar), **Moong**, **Urad**, **Cotton**, **Jute**, **Groundnut**, and **Soyabean**.
 
• The success of these crops is deeply linked to the **spatial and temporal distribution** of the monsoon rainfall across the Indian subcontinent.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rabi Season:**
 
 
• This season is known as the **winter cropping season**. Sowing begins in **October to December**, following the retreat of the monsoon.
 
• Harvesting occurs in the spring months of **April to June**. Key crops include **Wheat**, **Barley**, **Peas**, **Gram**, and **Mustard**.
 
 
 
• **Zaid Season:**
 
 
• It is a short season that falls between the **Rabi** and **Kharif** seasons, occurring during the summer months from **March to June**.
 
• Crops grown during this period include **Watermelon**, **Muskmelon**, **Cucumber**, various **Vegetables**, and **Fodder crops**.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Geography:**
 
 
• States like **Punjab**, **Haryana**, and **Western Uttar Pradesh** are major producers of Rabi crops like **Wheat** due to the success of the **Green Revolution** and availability of irrigation.
 
• Coastal regions like **Odisha**, **West Bengal**, and **Andhra Pradesh** are significant for Kharif crops like **Paddy**.
